topicName: boal and theatre of the oppressed

steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Forum theatre: a play is performed, then replayed with audience members ('spect-actors') stepping in to change the outcome — the audience becomes active. | Key Fact: Spect-actor: the audience member who stops the action and replaces a character — they are both spectator and actor. | Key Fact: Image theatre: participants use their bodies to create still images (sculptures) of oppression — reveals issues without words. | Key Fact: Invisible theatre: performed in public spaces without the audience knowing it's theatre — provokes real reactions and discussion.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how forum theatre works and why Boal believed it was important for social change. | What is the role of the 'Joker' in forum theatre? How does this differ from a traditional director? | Compare Boal's Theatre of the Oppressed with Brecht's epic theatre — both want social change but use different methods. How?
